transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-11
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Evan (CTO), Lara (Sr ML Eng), Samir (Infra), Priya (Product)

Summary (auto): quick discovery on Redwood PLG quickstart path, questions about hosted vs dedicated vs private, security requirements, and next steps to try free credits and run a small perf eval.

[00:00:00] Jordan: hey all, thanks for joining, i'm jordan from redwood, with maya our se, you guys good to run through quickstart and what you care about?
[00:00:10] Evan: yeah thanks, quick overview from our side - i'm evan, cto at sierra tech, we are building a customer support assistant on top of our ticketing data. goal is to go to prod in 3-4 months, start with hosted but will likely move to dedicated if volume ramps.
[00:00:28] Lara: yeah hi, i'm lara, i'll own the fine-tuning and model evaluation, main things: latency under 300ms for short prompts, cost per 1M tokens matters, and data residency for eu customers.
[00:00:42] Maya: awesome, that aligns w what we see. for quickstarts you can get time-to-first-token in under 15 minutes with our SDK and free credits, we have a quickstart repo and a one-click curl flow. (link to quickstart deck: https://redwood.ai/quickstart)
[00:01:00] Samir: curious about auth/ssO, we use okta across infra, what does redwood support?
[00:01:06] Jordan: we support SSO/SAML for enterprise, and api keys for self-serve. for private deployments we can integrate with customer idp. we'll share the security whitepaper.
[00:01:18] Lara: also curious about encrypt-at-rest and kms/hsm options. we need to know if we can bring our own key.
[00:01:24] Maya: yes we have KMS integrations and we support customer-managed keys for Private and Dedicated. Hosted has encryption at rest but if you need BYOK you'd look at Dedicated or Private.
[00:01:38] Evan: ok, that makes sense. what about model fallback and reliability if a region is down?
[00:01:44] Jordan: smart routing, you can set policies to failover to another region or to a cheaper variant. we also do automatic fallback to a compatible model variant when capacity's constrained.
[00:01:56] [00:02:10] Speaker 1: (muffled) question on cost math...
[00:02:15] Maya: on cost, for PLG self-serve you pay per-token; for Dedicated it's a reserved capacity model with commit tiers. we can run some estimates if you share traffic profile.
[00:02:28] Priya: timeline wise, if we start quickstart now, how fast can we evaluate RL and decide on dedicated? we want a POC in 4 weeks.
[00:02:36] Jordan: you can get dev traffic in within hours; with free credits we'll provision keys and you can hit our hosted API. for realistic perf, we usually run a small benchmark within 1-2 weeks then size Dedicated if needed.
[00:02:50] Lara: does quickstart include streaming and function calling support? we rely on structured outputs.
[00:02:55] Maya: yes streaming responses and function/tool calling are available via the SDK. example code in the repo, i can DM the snippet.
[00:03:05] [00:03:20] Evan: security review - we need SOC 2 and audit logs for compliance. do you provide audit trails per request?
[00:03:26] Jordan: we provide audit logs, RBAC, and we have SOC 2 + ISO in our security pack - will share the security pack PDF.
[00:03:34] Samir: for private deployments, is there an on-prem appliance or is it VPC only?
[00:03:39] Maya: both options exist; we have a VPC-hosted private control plane and an on-prem package for air-gapped environments. depends on what level of isolation you need.
[00:03:50] [00:04:05] Lara: wondering about latency targets - you mentioned 300ms; what about tail latency under load?
[00:04:10] Maya: latency SLOs are configurable per deployment. for small models and short prompts you can hit <200ms average in our hosted tier for EU region, but tail latency depends on batching and concurrency - that's where Dedicated helps.
[00:04:28] Jordan: also we do prefix/KV caching which helps repeated context. if your traffic has lots of repetitive prompts, it reduces tokens and cost.
[00:04:40] [00:05:00] Priya: what's the onboarding flow for quickstart? docs + sdk + sample prompts?
[00:05:05] Jordan: yes, quickstart has SDK for python/node, a curl example, and a sample prompts repo. time-to-first-token is often under 15 minutes from signup with free credits. i'll include the signup link.
[00:05:18] [00:06:00] Evan: any gotchas with our infra? we run k8s on aws, ephemeral instances, and have data in s3. we want to avoid moving data off-prem.
[00:06:08] Maya: for Hosted you send prompts to our api; for Dedicated we can set up a private subnet and peering, and for Private on-prem we can bring the runtime behind your network so data never leaves your vpc.
[00:06:22] [00:06:40] Samir: curious about quantization and throughput - do you offer int8 or cpu quantization so we can run cheaper?
[00:06:46] Maya: our runtime supports quantized execution paths and kernel selection per model; for cost-sensitive workloads we recommend certain quant profiles and we can recommend config per model and load.
[00:06:58] [00:07:15] Lara: who at redwood will help with evals?
[00:07:18] Jordan: se + solutions eng will support POC; maya will lead technical bench. my team will be point for commercial.
[00:07:28] [00:08:00] Jordan: ok let's do a quick walk through of the quickstart steps - maya you want to show code?
[00:08:05] Maya: sure, sample python paste: from redwood import Client, client = Client(api_key='REDACTED')... then client.chat.create with messages; streaming example uses websocket. (transcript note: code obfuscated)
[00:08:26] [00:08:45] Speaker 2: (overlap) is there a demo environment?
[00:08:48] Jordan: yes sandbox keys on sign-up with free credits. we also have a demo org we can put you in for testing.
[00:08:55] Priya: can we connect to our vector db for retrieval? we use milvus currently.
[00:09:01] Maya: we support embedding APIs and connectors; many customers use external vector stores like milvus/pinecone. we can show an example pipeline.
[00:09:12] [00:09:30] Evan: about pricing: if we do hosted initially what's the typical unit cost vs dedicated?
[00:09:36] Jordan: hosted is pay-as-you-go per token; dedicated has a monthly commit and lower per-token pricing plus predictable throughput. i'll send a pricing sheet, but rough rule: at sustained high volume Dedicated usually lowers unit cost 20-40% depending on commit and model.
[00:09:55] [00:10:20] Lara: ok for POC success criteria: 1) latency under 300ms median, 2) cost target <$X per 1M tokens (we'll define X), 3) data residency in EU, 4) accuracy vs current baseline.
[00:10:34] Jordan: sounds good. we'll capture that in the POC checklist.
[00:10:40] [00:11:05] Maya: we'll also run a small benchmark using your sample traffic to show throughput and tail latency; that will inform the Dedicated sizing. we'll need a 1-2 hour window of sample traffic or recorded traces.
[00:11:18] Samir: can we do a smoke test with 100 concurrent requests?
[00:11:22] Maya: yes we can simulate load; for Hosted we'll be mindful of quotas, but for Dedicated we can do real load tests once reserved capacity is provisioned.
[00:11:35] [00:12:00] Jordan: recap and next steps: jordan to send quickstart links + free credits, maya to schedule dedicated deep-dive, sierra to share sample dataset and traffic profile. we'll also share security docs and the pricing sheet.
[00:12:15] Evan: sounds great, let's target the bench eval next week.
[00:12:20] [00:12:30] Jordan: thanks everyone, i'll follow up after the call.
